title: USDA FSA Supplemental Disaster Relief Program (SDRP)
funding: Disaster relief payments; amount depends on eligible losses and program calculation
audience: Agricultural producers with eligible 2023 or 2024 revenue, quality, or production losses to crops, trees, bushes, or vines
summary: SDRP provides assistance for qualifying 2023 and 2024 disaster losses. Stage 1 covers indemnified losses using crop insurance or NAP data; Stage 2 can cover non-indemnified, uncovered, and quality losses.
verification_note: FSA's current SDRP page and August 10, 2026 announcement state that the deadline for both Stage 1 and Stage 2 is September 30, 2026.

summary: Current priorities include increasing use of Michigan agricultural products and regenerative practices for crops used in craft beverage production.

title: Michigan FSA Emergency Farm Loans — 2025 Drought, Heat, Frost/Freeze Designations
funding: Emergency farm credit; loan amount and terms depend on losses, security, eligibility, and repayment ability
audience: Eligible producers in designated primary or contiguous Michigan counties affected by specified 2025 drought/excessive heat and frost/freeze disasters

verification_note: Michigan FSA's April 8, 2026 designation notice lists October 13, 2026 as the application deadline for the cited drought/excessive heat and frost/freeze designations and enumerates primary and contiguous eligible counties.
